betterCitation: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, To the Reader, the opening sentence (trans. Donald M. Frame, 1957)
reason: Frame wording confirmed: This book was written in good faith, reader. It warns you from the outset that in it I have set myself no goal but a domestic and private one. That is Frame and no one else (Screech: You have here, Reader, a book whose faith can be trusted; Cotton: Reader, thou hast here an honest book), confirmed by web quotations of the Frame text and my own knowledge. Locator right (Au lecteur, first sentence). One fact to fix in the evidence, not in the source line: the Archive item completeessaysof0000mont is The Complete Essays of Montaigne, Stanford, 1958; Frame first published this rendering in The Complete Works of Montaigne, Stanford, 1957, so 1957 stands as the translation year but the evidence should name the Complete Works or say 1958 for the Complete Essays. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned; Essay is the form; 95 characters, no dash; opening line on the theme.
